note: Starter profile. Emergency numbers are filled in. Warning signs currently cover only stroke and heart attack (CDC); a general list is still needed. To be discussed and maintained by a community in this region. emergency.message: If you think you or someone else has a life-threatening emergency, call 911 now. Do not wait to book an appointment.

redFlags: Stroke: Sudden trouble walking, dizziness, loss of balance, or lack of coordination.
Stroke: Sudden numbness or weakness in the face, arm, or leg, especially on one side of the body.
Stroke: Sudden confusion, trouble speaking, or difficulty understanding speech.
Stroke: Sudden severe headache with no known cause.

Heart attack: Chest pain or discomfort. Most heart attacks involve discomfort in the center or left side of the chest that lasts for more than a few minutes or that goes away and comes back. The discomfort can feel like uncomfortable pressure, squeezing, fullness, or pain.
Heart attack: Feeling weak, light-headed, or faint. You may also break into a cold sweat.
Heart attack: Pain or discomfort in the jaw, neck, or back.
Heart attack: Pain or discomfort in one or both arms or shoulders.
Heart attack: Shortness of breath. This often comes along with chest discomfort, but shortness of breath also can happen before chest discomfort.
